github_issue.notes: The issue states a crisp, verifiable problem and every behavioral claim I checked matches the code: the registry deletes the server-side session and clears the cookie before building the redirect (registry/auth/routes.py:266-311), the hint is appended raw to the browser-facing URL (routes.py:302), and GET /oauth2/logout/{provider} accepts id_token_hint as a query param (auth_server/server.py:5624-5631). Acceptance criteria are genuinely testable (no hint in the redirect when the exchange succeeds, fallback on 404/5xx/timeout, provider-family URL parity, unauthenticated internal calls rejected), and the Out of Scope section explicitly names the residual IdP-hop exposure instead of overclaiming. The largest gap is that no acceptance criterion pins the metric API shape, which is where the implementation later broke. The #1503 reference and label names are unverifiable from the provided evidence.

lld.notes: This is the most repository-grounded LLD I could ask for: every anchor I checked is accurate (logout_handler at routes.py:237 with the hint block at 294-314, oauth2_logout at auth_server/server.py:5624, _is_redirect_within_cookie_domain at 928, internal_router gate at 1822, _trigger_auth_server_reload at scope_service.py:109, meters at 392-418, nginx /oauth2/logout/ at line 379), and the include_router-ordering discovery is real (include at server.py:4445 precedes where the new handler lands). The one material defect is in the load-bearing code sketch: `logout_hint_internal.inc(result="delivered")` contradicts the repo adapter, whose `inc(self, value: float = 1.0)` takes no label kwargs (registry/observability/_compat.py:55) - the established idiom is `.labels(result=...).inc()` (e.g. registry/core/telemetry.py:819) - and the implementer copied the bug verbatim. Minor: the counter description mentions an `error` label that no code path ever emits. Alternatives, rollout both directions, and rollback are all committed, not waved at.

review.notes: This is a real review, not role-play: it disagrees with the draft five times on concrete, verifiable grounds (the 5.0s timeout precedent checks out at registry/auth/routes.py:153; the single-use jti and mcp-internal audience at registry/auth/internal.py:42,164-190; the dead Referer branch; the helper-returns-Optional change) and tracks each resolution into the revised LLD. The post-review addendum about include_router copying routes at call time is technically correct and was confirmed against the source. Its largest miss is that the SMTS reviewer discussed counter semantics (Sage-2) without checking the counter call API, so the `inc(result=...)` defect in the LLD's own code sketch passed through all five personas. No finding was manufactured; none of the praised claims I spot-checked was false.

testing.notes: The plan tests the exact behavior the issue promised, with real oracles: 303 Location contents byte-identical to the legacy URL on fallback, provider parity across all four families, 404/401/timeout/connection/garbage-body failure modes, a backwards-compat matrix covering both old-new deployment orders, a WAF-rule simulation, an nginx access-log grep oracle, and rollback verification. Paths and conventions agree with the repo (tests/unit/auth/ and tests/auth_server/unit/ exist, asyncio_mode=auto in pyproject.toml:127, the /internal/* unauthenticated-rejection meta-test at tests/auth_server/unit/test_server.py:1335-1390). The metric name matches the patch. Weaker spots: `uv sync --extra dev`, the port numbers, and the ASGITransport convention claim are unverified, and the planned counter assertions would have exposed the implementation's inc() API misuse had they been written and run.

implementation.notes: The patch faithfully realizes the revised LLD across all five files: the removed provider-param block matches auth_server/server.py:5677-5716 character-for-character, the internal endpoint inherits the verified validate_internal_auth gate, and the include_router move is sound and automatically covered by the existing meta-test. Two material defects: (1) `logout_hint_internal.inc(result="delivered"/"fallback")` raises TypeError because _CounterAdapter.inc() accepts only `value` (registry/observability/_compat.py:55) - inside logout_handler's broad `except Exception` this silently converts every hinted OAuth2 logout into a local-only /login redirect, reintroducing the exact SSO-survives regression the task exists to fix on both the new and the fallback path; (2) `git apply --check` fails on the final hunk (patch context reads "legacy scope audit" where the file has "legacy-scope audit" at the _run_legacy_scope_audit_on_startup docstring), directly contradicting implementation.md's "Verified: git apply --check passes at 5f725c1d". The summary is otherwise honest about skipping the two promised test files, which is precisely the coverage that would have caught defect (1); both fixes are one token and one character, but as submitted the change does not apply cleanly and breaks the main path at runtime.

verdict: An exceptionally well-grounded design suite (issue, LLD, review, and testing plan all verified against the repository at the line-number level) whose implementation undermines it with a runtime-breaking counter-API misuse on the logout main path and a patch that does not actually apply despite the summary's verified-applies claim.
